## youtube-poster
Webhook-triggered posting workflow for YouTube, dispatched by the backend (`service/n8n.ts` → `buildYouTubePayload`). Unlike Graph API/Threads, YouTube Data API v3 can't just be handed a URL — it needs the actual video bytes uploaded via a **resumable upload session** (init call → PUT the bytes to the returned Location URL).

**OAuth is entirely the backend's job.** n8n only ever receives an already-fresh `access_token` (the backend swaps the stored refresh token for one right before dispatch — `RefreshStrategy.ON_DEMAND`). refresh_token/client_id/secret never touch n8n.

**SUCCESS ≠ published.** The callback fires as soon as the PUT finishes, while YouTube is still processing (`uploadStatus: uploaded`). The backend's video-status poller (`queue/video-status-worker.ts`) polls `videos.list?part=status` and only then marks the post PUBLISHED or FAILED (rejected/duplicate/etc.).

Because the video bytes (Download Video) and the upload session URL (Initiate Resumable Upload) come from two independent HTTP calls, they run in parallel and a **Merge** node combines them before the final binary PUT.

⚠️ Known gap (websitePlan.md §3): the whole video is downloaded into n8n before the upload starts — streaming-relay fix planned once S3 exists.

**Callbacks** send `x-callback-secret: $env.CALLBACK_SECRET` — must match backend `N8N_CALLBACK_SECRET`.

Manual test payload:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/youtube-poster \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "post_id": "pst_test004",
    "user_id": "usr_test",
    "platform": "youtube",
    "media_type": "VIDEO",
    "media_urls": ["https://.../video.mp4"],
    "youtube_metadata": {
      "title": "Test upload",
      "description": "Testing youtube-poster",
      "privacy": "private",
      "made_for_kids": false,
      "tags": ["smposting"],
      "category_id": "22"
    },
    "token": { "access_token": "YOUR_VALID_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN" },
    "callback_url": "https://webhook.site/your-id"
  }'
```

`privacy` defaults to `private` if omitted. `media_type: SHORTS` is informational here — the backend already appended `#Shorts` to the description; YouTube itself decides Shorts from aspect ratio/duration (vertical or square, ≤3 min).

**Verify after import:** 'Upload Video Binary' Body Content Type = 'n8n Binary File', field `data`.
